calls.head: Carolina feeds on loose pucks
calls.body: Carolina ranks 3rd of 32 for chances off turnovers (7.8% of its chances come right after winning the puck); Washington ranks 32nd for avoiding breakdowns.
calls.call: At least its usual 7.8% of Carolina’s 5-on-5 chances come right after winning the puck.

calls.happened: 4.2% of Carolina’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against its usual 7.8%.

calls.head: Penalties could cost Washington
calls.body: Carolina’s power play creates 8.0 expected goals per 60, 7th in the league. Washington’s penalty kill ranks 26th.
calls.call: Carolina’s power play creates at least its usual 8.0 expected goals per 60.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 69% chance, but Washington had other ideas.

WSH.head: We gave Washington a 31% chance, and Washington proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Washington leaned on its bottom six
surprises.body: Washington’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against its usual 41% and a league average of 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Washington got to the dangerous areas
surprises.body: Washington needed 10.5 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 15.5 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 45 games.
